# Dependency policy source of truth (proposal-ci-cd-release-engineering.md §5.2).
#
# Routine PRs run `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` (advisories stay a
# separate security signal so a new RustSec advisory against an unchanged
# Cargo.lock doesn't redden an unrelated PR). Release qualification runs the
# full `cargo deny check`, including advisories.
#
# License allow-list is exactly what knowledge/evidence/ci-slice1-baseline-2026-08-17.md
# measured against the unmodified graph: 27 distinct expressions across 409
# resolved package versions, all ordinary permissive/public-domain terms.
# `LGPL-2.1-or-later` — the one entry the baseline flagged as worth a specific

# look rather than blanket admission — is deliberately NOT allowed here; see
# the comment below.

[advisories]
db-path = "~/.cargo/advisory-db"
db-urls = ["https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db"]
yanked = "deny"

# S4 Y2 (G3, gate a): scoped, dated exception for a single named advisory,
# not a broadened rule and not a disabled gate.
#
# RUSTSEC-2026-0192 — `ttf-parser` 0.25.1 is unmaintained, no safe upgrade.
# Reached unconditionally via anydoc -> pdf-inspector -> lopdf -> ttf-parser
# (font metadata for `pdf-inspector`'s PDF leg; `anydoc` ships no feature
# flag to drop `pdf-inspector` from the build). Recorded/reverted spike:
# tests/fixtures/anydoc_corpus/SPIKE-G3.md.
#
# Owner ruling (J4), 2026-08-27:
# knowledge/rulings/owner-rulings/anydoc-adoption-2026-08-27.md — ADOPT

# anydoc; the advisory is accepted risk in a pre-alpha, open-source, MIT
# harness because per-format composition would defeat the "any doc"
# capability itself (A1 §6.3). The ruling's condition (2) is a
# replaceability boundary — anydoc lives behind a narrow adapter contract
# so it stays swappable; that is proved structurally by this wave's
# one-owner adapter test, not by this file.
#
# This entry ignores exactly this one advisory ID. It does NOT ignore the
# `ttf-parser` crate, the `anydoc`/`pdf-inspector`/`lopdf` crates, or any
# other advisory ID — cargo-deny's `ignore` list matches by RUSTSEC ID, so a
# different advisory reaching the graph through the same subtree (a new ID

# against ttf-parser, lopdf, pdf-inspector, anydoc, or anything else the
# anydoc dependency edge pulls in) still fails `cargo deny check` under this
# same config. Proven, not just asserted, against this exact file, by
# `tests/fixtures/anydoc_corpus/prove-exception-is-scoped.sh` (rerunnable;
# last recorded run: `tests/fixtures/anydoc_corpus/G3-exception-narrowness-proof.md`) —
# it runs `cargo deny check advisories` against THIS file with a synthetic
# advisory injected against `lopdf` (a sibling of `ttf-parser` under
# `anydoc -> pdf-inspector -> lopdf`) under a fresh id this entry has never
# heard of, and asserts that advisory still fails the gate while
# RUSTSEC-2026-0192 stays ignored.
#

# Revisit triggers (ruling, "Revisit triggers" section — any one reopens
# this decision):
# - an `anydoc`/`pdf-inspector` release drops or replaces `ttf-parser`, or a
#   `ttf-parser` release resolves RUSTSEC-2026-0192 with a safe upgrade;
# - a NEW advisory arrives through the anydoc subtree (by design, this
#   entry will not suppress it — the gate goes red and that redness is the
#   trigger firing, not a bug in this exception);
# - `anydoc` itself becomes unmaintained, at which point the replaceability
#   boundary is what gets exercised.
#
# NOT covered by this entry: the pre-existing, unrelated yanked `chacha20`
# via `ulid` -> `rand` (sergeant-rs#328) stays a live failure of its own —

# this exception does not touch it and does not suppress it.
# S5 W3b (F5, gate 1): a SECOND scoped, dated exception for a single named
# advisory. It sits beside the anydoc entry above and does not touch,
# generalise or replace it — two named IDs, not a relaxed rule.
#
# RUSTSEC-2024-0436 — `paste` 1.0.15 is unmaintained and archived; the
# advisory itself says "No safe upgrade is available!". Reached
# unconditionally via `paste -> tokenizers 0.21.4 -> model2vec-rs 0.2.1`,
# and A2 §6's semantic half needs a Model2Vec implementation (decision
# A2-06). Verified unavoidable rather than asserted, in
# tests/fixtures/model2vec_corpus/SPIKE-F5.md:
#   - `paste` is NOT optional in `tokenizers 0.21.4` — no `optional = true`,

#     no feature guard, so no feature combination drops it;
#   - `tokenizers 0.23.1` still depends on it;
#   - `model2vec-rs` requires `tokenizers = "0.21"` regardless;
#   - the alternative crate `model2vec 0.3.0` requires the same.
#   Every Rust Model2Vec reads `tokenizer.json` through `tokenizers`, and
#   `tokenizers` goes through `paste`.
#
# Owner ruling (J4), 2026-08-30:
# knowledge/rulings/owner-rulings/model2vec-paste-advisory-2026-08-30.md —
# "Model2Vec is ADOPTED — it always was (A2-06) … RUSTSEC-2024-0436 is
# accepted as a SCOPED, DATED cargo-deny exception naming that advisory ID
# specifically — never a broadened rule, never a disabled gate … The next
# advisory must still fail the gate."
#

# NOT excepted, and must never be: **RUSTSEC-2025-0119** (`number_prefix` via
# `indicatif` via `tokenizers/progressbar`). It is AVOIDED, not ignored —
# `Cargo.toml` declares `tokenizers` directly with `fancy-regex` alone, which
# drops `indicatif`/`number_prefix` from `Cargo.lock` entirely. The ruling's
# decision 3 is explicit: "The second advisory stays avoided, not excepted."
# `tests/w3b_model2vec_manifest_pin.rs` fails if either crate reappears in
# the lockfile.
#
# Scoped by ID, and PROVEN so rather than asserted, against this exact file,
# by `tests/fixtures/model2vec_corpus/prove-exception-is-scoped.sh`
# (rerunnable; last recorded run:
# tests/fixtures/model2vec_corpus/F5-exception-narrowness-proof.md) — it runs

# `cargo deny check advisories` against THIS file with a synthetic advisory
# injected against `tokenizers` (the crate directly between `paste` and
# `model2vec-rs`) under a fresh id this entry has never heard of, and asserts
# that advisory still fails the gate while RUSTSEC-2024-0436 stays ignored.
#
# Revisit triggers (ruling, "Revisit triggers" — any one reopens this):
# - a `tokenizers` release that drops or replaces `paste`;
# - a `paste` release resolving the advisory;
# - a NEW advisory arriving through the model2vec subtree — by design this
#   entry will not suppress it, and the gate going red IS the trigger firing.

ignore = [
  { id = "RUSTSEC-2026-0192", reason = "anydoc's pdf-inspector->lopdf leg pulls unmaintained ttf-parser unconditionally; accepted risk per owner ruling knowledge/rulings/owner-rulings/anydoc-adoption-2026-08-27.md (J4), scoped to this one advisory ID only — see the comment above for revisit triggers." },
  { id = "RUSTSEC-2024-0436", reason = "model2vec-rs -> tokenizers pulls unmaintained/archived paste unconditionally (no safe upgrade); accepted risk per owner ruling knowledge/rulings/owner-rulings/model2vec-paste-advisory-2026-08-30.md (J4), scoped to this one advisory ID only — see the comment above for revisit triggers." },
]

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
wildcards = "deny"

[licenses]
allow = [
  "MIT",
  "Apache-2.0",
  "BSD-2-Clause",
  "BSD-3-Clause",
  "ISC",
  "Zlib",
  "CC0-1.0",
  "Unlicense",
  "Unicode-3.0",
  "CDLA-Permissive-2.0",
]
confidence-threshold = 0.8

# LGPL-2.1-or-later appears once in the graph, inside an OR clause on a
# dependency in the windows-sys/icu-adjacent cluster (baseline §3). Left off
# the allow-list on purpose: it's the one expression in the measured set that
# isn't a permissive/public-domain-style license, and it hasn't had an owner
# ruling to admit it. Verified with `cargo deny check licenses` against this
# allow-list: the crate's OR clause resolves to an already-allowed sibling
# term, so `licenses ok` holds without adding LGPL-2.1-or-later here. If a

# future dependency bump drops that sibling term from the OR clause, this
# check starts failing on it — that failure is the intended fail-closed
# behavior, not a regression to silently work around.

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"

# --- chunker-utf8 density extension (S6 wave) — synthetic, appended for
# fixture coverage only; the content above this line is the REAL
# sergeant-rs deny.toml, verbatim, and is what reproduced the original
# panic at byte 3592 (see brief-chunker-utf8.md). This block adds the
# additional multi-byte forms the wave brief names that deny.toml alone
# does not contain: accented words, CJK, and an emoji.
#
# Accented: café, naïve, façade, jalapeño, Zürich, résumé — six words.
# CJK: 你好世界 ("hello world"), 東京 ("Tokyo"), 数据库 ("database").
# Emoji: a lock 🔒, a check ✅, and a warning ⚠️ — three graphemes, each
# a multi-byte.
#

# NOTE (F-IN-02): an earlier revision of this comment claimed the lock and
# check together straddle a byte offset that is an exact multiple of
# chunk::DESIRED_CHUNK_LENGTH (750). That is false of the committed golden:
# tree-sitter's TOML grammar always splits chunks at comment/node edges, so
# the AST-merge path cannot naturally land a chunk boundary mid-codepoint —
# every byte_start/byte_end in sample_multibyte.toml.golden.json already
# lands on a valid char boundary, and the lock/check pair sits entirely
# inside one chunk (bytes 8082..8791), straddling nothing. This fixture
# exercises non-ASCII density and round-trip content fidelity through the
# real pipeline; the mid-codepoint boundary-snapping invariant itself is

# proven directly, by construction, in `chunk.rs`'s
# `finalize_chunk_never_panics_on_a_boundary_that_splits_a_multibyte_char`
# and `finalize_chunk_never_duplicates_content_across_adjacent_boundaries_
# sharing_a_split_point` — not by this file landing on a real chunk seam.
#
[extension.metadata]
note = "Zürich → 東京 — one em dash, one arrow, both multi-byte"
